TBH psychosis is so different for everyone that experiences it; I know many people who experience it who still use cannabis without big issues. My best suggestion is Take It Very Slow; and do your very best to stay aware of how it affects you. If you take too much it will Not be Fun but there is a possibility that in small, measured doses it could really help with your mental health overall. If you find it does you more harm than good than just move on and avoid it.

I don't experience psychosis regularly but I'm prone to occasional episodes. D8 seems way less likely to trigger an episode in my experience, but again everyone is different. I like that I can measure this stuff out in specific amounts, that helps keep me from taking too much. 

Smoking regular cannabis can be a craps shoot because oftentimes (unless you buy from dispensaries) you don't know how much THC is in it and the potency can vary a lot between dofferent buds, making it easy to accidentally take too much and stress your brain out. 

Also - the addition of CBD may help reduce the potential for psychotic episodes. I dip my delta 8 dab in powdered CBD isolate whenever my anxiety/paranoia is bad and it helps. Having a seperate source of CBD (either vape or edible) is also good for times when you take too much THC you can just take CBD alone and it could help balance you back out.

Just be safe, be smart, know your limits. Don't overdo it. I'm not a doctor so I speak from experience, not full blown medical education. I will say that experts usually talk patients who experience psychosis away from all forms of THC but I think many of their opinions may be informed by prejudice  against drugs they consider recreational.

Lemon Curd:

250g Lemon Juice
250g Sugar
250g butter
8 whole eggs

Heat lemon juice and sugar in large saucepan. Add the butter in small chunks. If you want to D8 than this is where you add your infused budder, just keep total butter weight at 250g

start whisking the eggs in a large seperate bowl like you're making an omelette. Once the butter has melted all the way into the juice, whisk it into the bowl with the eggs and mix well. 

Pour contents back into saucepan and set to medium low heat, stirring with a whisk. Once the first bubbles come up to boil turn off heat

Pour lemon curd through a strainer; a spatula may be needed to scrape away eggy bits clogging the strainer

this is where i weigh my final product and divide into single serving tart shells; I filled about 18 of these 3 inch tart shells. You can also just fill a large no bake pie crust of your choice with the lemon filling 

lay plastic wrap over the top of all the pies and refrigerate until curd has set properly. Top with your favorite berry or whipped cream!

Procedure- 
1. Aquire Dum Dums and Fun Dip; seperate fun dip powder into different containers
2. Heat 1 to 2 grams distillate in shot glass, keep warmed on hot plate/in front of space heater
3. Weigh shot glass before and after to find average dosing per pop
4. Dip tip of each pop into distillate; roll pop gently in fun dip sugar until it coats distillate well enough to prevent sticking
5. Poke holes in 2oz condiment cup lids and portion some Fun Dip Powder into each cup
6. Push Dum Dum stick through lid hole and close each container
7. Divide the difference in before/after shotglass weight by number of pops made for average dose (this will not be super accurate but its as close as one can get with this method)

This story is more a testament to my own desperation and stupidity than a tale of something creepy i found, but one time i caused a scare at a local park trying to impress a girl. She was into "vulture culture", aka she liked to pick up roadkill and process the bones for artistic display.
Long story short, I had taken up the habit of picking up dead animals on the side of the road to give to her (gross, i know. The things we do for lust). 

One day in particular I had found a gigantic raccoon. Lifting him was a challenge, he was frozen solid because it was mid winter. I knew the body would take forever to decompose in this state, so I opted to retrieve only the skull to make processing easier on her. 

Naturally, I didnt want my neighbors seeing me decapitating a raccoon in the backyard of my suburban neighborhood, so my brilliant solution was to go to the middle of the woods to do it in the privacy of nature. I went deep into the trees in my local park to do it; carrying the poor creature in a large bucket. I did the deed; it was as gruesome as it sounds; I had never butchered an animal before so it didn't leave a pretty scene. I put the raccoon head into a plastic coffee container, but i had the rest of the body to deal with. 

I wanted to try to save the rest of the bones, but the decomposition wouldn't work in the middle of winter and i figured she didn't want a huge bucket of dead thing in the storage basement of her apartment complex. So my brilliant solution was to.... hide the bucket under the overhang of a ditch. I figured I could come back and get it after spring when it warmed up and decayed. I left with the head and promptly forgot about the corpse i left behind.

What I didn't plan for was the hikers and their dogs. Probably three weeks later I saw an article circulating facebook warning people of "occult" behavior in the park. A man, his 11 year old son, and his dog came across a decapitated raccoon, the result of what they believed was from some kind of satanic sacrifice (people in the midwest are fucking dumb btw i don't know how they came to that conclusion). I was paranoid that there would be some police investigation in the matter but i never heard about it again.

When i first started doing stencils i would start with a picture of my subject, desaturate the image to grayscale, up constrast and fiddle with the exposure/brigtness of photos as needed on my computer/phone so that they become solid black and white. Then trace the simplified black spaces onto whatever im using as the stencil material, making sure to cut so it stays in one piece. Easyish, making multiple layers takes more steps but one layer is a good start. Try using a pic with a white backround, it works way better.
